title: Cozy Market Atlas
methodology: Compiled on 3–4 Oct 2026 from Steam Page Analyzer, GameDiscoverCo, How To Market A Game, VG Insights, Gamalytic and Raijin estimates, publisher and developer statements, and press coverage. Every figure carries a source link and a confidence level. Page fetches were blocked in the research environment, so figures were taken from search-result summaries of the cited pages; spot-check any number before you put money behind it. Third-party Steam sales estimates often disagree with each other by 2–5x.
howToUpdate: Edit the JSON files in data/: games.json for games, niches.json for gaps, market.json for trends and benchmarks, playbook.json for operations, concepts.json for game ideas, insights.json for the headline findings.
Run python3 scripts/validate_data.py to catch missing or malformed fields.
Run python3 scripts/build.py to rebuild the single-file dashboard in dist/.
Steam review counts and prices refresh every Monday through the GitHub Action (scripts/refresh_steam.py). You can also run the script yourself.
Once a quarter, ask Claude to re-run the cozy market research and update data/, then add a line to this change log.

changelog.note: Proven genres: research on first-person craft and shop sims, top-down management and other evergreen cozy genres (hits, misses, saturation, open themes). Five new suggestions on proven loops (Well Loved, Glaze Day, Stem & Ribbon, Soak & Snooze, Tidepool Lane). New 'Proven demand' factor; originality weighs less; new default preset 'Solo + AI, proven genre → Steam'.
Custom weights moved up next to the 'Rank for' buttons (a Custom button opens them); the Briefing links to them and says when your custom weights are in use.
Saved ideas keep a full copy of the plan or Idea lab write-up as it was when you saved it, and say when the dashboard's version has changed or been removed since.

Saved tab: save any game suggestion, Idea lab idea or chat answer, add your own ideas, and keep notes on each. On claude.ai they're stored with the dashboard on your account; the chat knows what you've saved.
Every box (cards, callouts, suggestions, panels, chat answers) has a Copy button that copies its text without the buttons.

Idea lab: 80 ideas generated from four lenses, scored by two independent judges, top 12 critiqued by a player/market critic and a build/distribution critic. Five finalists (Leaflings, If It Fits, Lemon Ink, Cuttings, Fold Together) added with full plans. New scoring factors: originality and fit for a solo creator.

Removed time estimates: plans are now ordered steps with the signal to move on, the 90-day plan is 'Your first steps', and ladder stages have no durations. Platform rules (e.g. Steam's 30-day wait) and measured facts stay.

Added the shipping ladder (ship & test → first money → reach → graduate) with move-up and kill signals, and each game's path up it. Steam is now the top step for proven PC-suited games, not the default.

Every suggestion now has a Look & feel section: an 'imagine' description, a screen-layout walkthrough, named color palette, visual references, shapes, characters, camera, lighting, textures, interface, type, motion, sound, the key screenshot and clip, what to avoid, and a copyable art brief for an illustrator.

Added trends outside games: 47 culture signals across collectibles and aesthetics, wellness and hobbies, and social/search/seasonal, a launch calendar, a 'Cultural tailwind' scoring factor, and a new suggestion (Treat Box). Culture ideas folded into the other five web-first concepts.

Re-aimed at a solo, AI-assisted, web-first cozy business: new Launch & grow and What spreads pages (platforms, monetization, TikTok/YouTube marketing, viral hits, AI rules), five new web-first game suggestions, scoring presets (Solo + AI vs. Small studio), and a fact-check of 15 key figures (12 confirmed, 3 revised).
Five main game suggestions (new: Terraces), each with the market signals that drive it and a characteristics spec; side-by-side comparison; Roblox and desktop-idle ideas moved to side bets.
Added the Briefing (seven decisions and a 90-day plan), the Outliers page, 'So what' takeaways on every page, and Ask the Atlas, a chat that answers from this data.
First edition: 57 games, 26 niches, 15 trends, 21 benchmarks, 13 publishers and 6 ranked game concepts.
